prompt: Scope: backend only. Implement these exact behaviors for POST /api/v1/items/ and PUT /api/v1/items/{id} (do not change existing permission or description rules). Core rule summary: before any validation or storage, remove only ASCII space characters (U+0020) from the start and end of the incoming title string; then measure length by Unicode code points; allowed length is 3 through 80 inclusive. Create (POST) must include a title; update (PUT) may omit title to leave stored value unchanged; an explicitly provided null for title (in either POST or PUT) must always yield HTTP 422. The backend must store and return the processed (trimmed) title value. Implementation steps: 1) Request parsing: accept JSON body as before. Detect three title states: absent (no title property in parsed JSON), explicit null (title present with null), or present string. 2) Title handling rules: - If title is explicit null: respond 422 Unprocessable Entity with a validation error for the title field. - If handling POST: if title is absent or explicit null, respond 422 (creation requires title). - If handling PUT: if title is absent, do not modify the stored title; continue handling other fields and permissions as currently implemented. If title is present as a string, continue below. 3) Trimming: when title is present as a string, strip only U+0020 characters from both ends. Do NOT strip other Unicode whitespace (e.g., NBSP U+00A0, TAB, newline) unless current contracts already required that (spec says only U+0020). Perform this trim before any other processing or validation. 4) Length measurement: count Unicode code points in the trimmed string and validate that the count is between 3 and 80 inclusive. Use language-appropriate, code-point-aware routines (examples: in Python 3 len(s) counts code points; in Java use s.codePointCount(0, s.length()); in JavaScript use [...s].length or Array.from(s).length to count code points rather than s.length). 5) Validation failures: if the trimmed string has length <3 or >80, respond 422 with a validation error associated to the title field and a clear reason (too short or too long). If the trimmed string is empty (e.g., input was all U+0020 spaces), this will fail as length <3. 6) Storage and response: on success (POST or PUT when title present and valid), persist the trimmed title into the data store and include the trimmed title in the response payload exactly as stored. Do not re-introduce leading/trailing U+0020 characters when returning. 7) PUT semantics: ensure that when title is omitted from the request body, the stored title remains unchanged and the response reflects the existing stored (possibly previously trimmed) value. 8) Error codes: use 422 Unprocessable Entity for all title validation and required-field failures described above. Maintain the same response format/shape used elsewhere in the API for validation errors. 9) Tests to add (unit + integration + acceptance): include explicit cases: - POST with title trimmed length 2 -> expect 422. - POST with title trimmed length 3 -> expect success. - POST with title trimmed length 80 -> expect success. - POST with title trimmed length 81 -> expect 422. - POST with title equal to only U+0020 spaces -> expect 422. - POST missing title -> expect 422. - PUT with no title property -> existing title unchanged. - PUT with title explicit null -> expect 422. - PUT with title present and trimmed length valid -> stored and returned trimmed. For each success case assert that the returned/stored title equals the trimmed string. 10) Audit & backwards-compatibility: do not change permission checks or description validation logic; only apply these rules to the title field. 11) Logging and observability: log validation failures for title with enough context to reproduce requests, but do not log raw request bodies in production if sensitive. 12) Documentation: update backend API documentation to state: trimming of leading/trailing U+0020 is performed server-side before validation; length is counted in Unicode code points; POST requires title; PUT may omit title; explicit null is invalid. 13) Deployment: include migration/compatibility review if any clients currently expect untrimmed titles; if no contract exists, still proceed but document the change. Acceptance criteria (must pass automated tests): - 2/81 characters -> fail (422). - 3/80 characters -> succeed. - All-space input -> fail. - Update with omitted title -> stored title unchanged. - Explicit null -> 422. Ensure stored and returned titles are the trimmed values.
